messages:
jess: FYI — ACME (acme-123) reported that their dashboard shows 0 hourly usage rows for the past 6 hours. Customer says billing UI looks wrong and is asking for an explanation. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/acme-missing-hours.png :rotating_light:

support-bot: alert: hourly-rollup-backfill failed for tenant=acme-123 at 2026-03-16T22:03:12Z, job_id=fb-9a7, exit_code=137, reason=OOM

mike: putting on infra-oncall. Can someone grab the backfill logs and consumer lag? Suspect the backfill job died mid-upsert and left gaps.

tara: I pulled the backfill logs from the runner pod. seeing repeated db constraint errors then OOM. snippet:

```
2026-03-16T22:02:58Z ERROR backfill_runner.py:245 Upsert failed: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "hourly_usage_pkey"
DETAIL:  Key (tenant_id, hour)=(acme-123, 2026-03-16T16:00:00Z) already exists.
2026-03-16T22:03:12Z ERROR backfill_runner.py:312 OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
```

This looks like the backfill retried a chunk that partially wrote rows, then hit a duplicate on retry, then OOM killed the pod. The upsert path currently does INSERT-only which causes duplicate failure and abort.

natalie: I reproduced locally by running the same backfill window for acme-123 (14:00-20:00 UTC). Got the same duplicate pkey then no further writes when the process crashed. Repro steps:
1) k8s exec into backfill-runner
2) `python backfill.py --tenant acme-123 --start 2026-03-16T14:00 --end 2026-03-16T20:00`

Result: process exits with code 137 after ~45m; DB shows missing hours 16:00-18:00 as zero rows.

mike: quick mitigation options:
- re-run backfill with dedupe/skip flag (fast) OR
- change upsert to `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` so retries are idempotent (safer).

infra-oncall: I'll spin up a scaled backfill worker with higher heap and requeue the job. Also can patch the SQL to use ON CONFLICT. Will coordinate with Tara for patch.

mike: patch created: `backfill_runner: use ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, hour) DO UPDATE SET tokens = EXCLUDED.tokens` — pushing to staging for smoke.

tara: tested patch locally, idempotent now, duplicate inserts become updates and do not fail. Also reduced memory footprint by batching 500->200. Patch LGTM.

infra-oncall: requeued backfill job fb-9a7 -> fb-9a7-rerun with patched runner and bigger heap. Watching consumer offsets and DB writes. Commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n etl logs backfill-runner-fb-9a7-rerun -f
psql -c "SELECT hour, count(*) FROM hourly_usage WHERE tenant_id='acme-123' AND hour >= '2026-03-16T14:00:00Z' GROUP BY hour ORDER BY hour;"
```

Initial snapshot (before rerun):
```
2026-03-16 22:10:00 | 14:00 | 12
2026-03-16 22:10:00 | 15:00 | 10
2026-03-16 22:10:00 | 16:00 | 0
2026-03-16 22:10:00 | 17:00 | 0
2026-03-16 22:10:00 | 18:00 | 3
```

Monitoring updates over the next 70 minutes showed the missing hours filling in. At 23:45 UTC counts are: 16:00 -> 98, 17:00 -> 102. Dashboard repopulated after the next metrics rollup.

jess: Confirmed with customer that their dashboard now shows expected numbers; billing UI reconciled. Customer notified with root cause summary and the action (idempotent upsert + rerun).

mike: will open a rollout PR to make the idempotent upsert the default for all backfill runners and add a healthcheck to terminate if memory > 80% to avoid partial commits.

jess: Thanks everyone — marking this as resolved on our side. I'll update the support ticket and close the incident. :white_check_mark:
